**WARNING:** `checkAnnotations` lost the per-run error handling from the ported source — one failed annotations fetch discards the entire map.

The original (`fetchPrActState` in act/github.ts:223–229) wrapped each `failureAnnotations()` call in try/catch and degraded per-check: a transient rate limit or network error only marked that one check as unknown. This port has no catch inside the loop, so a single `gh api .../annotations` failure throws out of `checkAnnotations` and all counts accumulated so far are lost. The facade contract (core/review.ts:103–106) documents the absent key as the benign "no annotations endpoint" case and says nothing about throwing, so the failure mode is also undocumented. A non-array error payload (e.g. `{"message":"..."}`) would additionally make `pages.flat()` throw a TypeError. Consider catching per run and omitting the failed key, so callers degrade per-check like they do today.

**WARNING:** `mergedPrInfo` fabricates the current timestamp when `mergedAt` is null.

After the `state !== 'MERGED'` guard above, a MERGED PR with null `mergedAt` is a GitHub API inconsistency — but silently substituting `new Date().toISOString()` produces a plausible-but-wrong timestamp that flows into date-window filtering and last-N sorting downstream (`filterByMergedDate`/`applyLastN` in debt), landing the PR in the wrong harvest window or as the newest entry. Throwing like the not-merged case would fail loudly instead of corrupting data silently. (Inherited from debt/github.ts:123, so not a regression — but the facade is the new contract boundary and this is the moment to decide.)

body:
**WARNING:** `explicitMergedPrs` catch-all collapses infrastructure failures into per-PR "fetch failed — skipped".

`ghJson` throws for every failure mode — bad auth, network outage, rate limit, `gh` not installed — and this catch turns all of them into a stderr warning plus `continue`. A batch of 20 ids with an unauthenticated `gh` yields 20 warnings and an empty return, indistinguishable from "all ids unmerged". Per the repo's gate rule (infra failures never block, project findings do), these should be distinguishable: at minimum include the error text in the warning, or rethrow non-PR-specific failures.

body:
**SUGGESTION:** The label-boundary match still claims right-edge subdomain lookalikes, contrary to the doc comment.

`host.split('.').includes('github')` returns true for `github.com.evil.com` (labels `['github','com','evil','com']`) or `foo.github.attacker.tld` — the comment above promises "but not lookalikes (evilgithub.com)", which only holds for left-edge lookalikes. Low impact today since `gh` would fail closed against an unauthenticated host, but the boundary is asymmetric versus the documented contract, and no test covers this shape. A suffix check like `host === 'github.com' || host.endsWith('.github.com') || host.includes('.github.')` (or matching a GHES allowlist) would honor the comment.

**SUGGESTION:** Hand-rolled PR link instead of `prLink()` from `@bro/core`.

The repo convention (AGENTS.md) is that user-facing PR references are formatted by `prLink()` in `@bro/core`, which the old debt code used here (`pull request ${prLink(ownerRepo, pr)} not found`). This port re-inlines the format at lines 194, 268, and 323. Output is byte-identical today, but single-sourcing keeps the convention intact if the format ever changes — `prLink` is already exported from `@bro/core` and the package already imports from it.

**SUGGESTION:** `explicitMergedPrs` doesn't deduplicate `ids`; duplicates produce duplicate rows.

The old pipeline deduplicated upstream — `parseCsvInts` (debt/github.ts:187–192) ran every part through a `seen` set before `fetchExplicitMergedPrs` was reached. The new facade accepts `ids: number[]` directly with no dedup, so `mergedPrs(ref, { ids: [12, 12] })` returns the same `MergedPr` twice, double-counting in any consumer aggregation. The contract boundary moved to the facade but the dedup guarantee didn't; dedupe here or document the uniqueness requirement on `MergedPrQuery.ids`.

**SUGGESTION:** `ThreadPage` types `line` as `number | undefined` though GraphQL emits null.

GitHub's `PullRequestReviewComment.line` is a nullable `Int` and is commonly null for file-level comments; the old debt type modeled this as `line?: number | null`. The normalizer at line 232 (`c.line ?? null`) handles it correctly, so there's no runtime bug — but the inline type misleads future readers of `ThreadPage` into thinking the field is always present when non-undefined.
